assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organisation as phase separation of driven, non-equilibrium droplets. Statistical-physics concepts (surface tension, nucleation, active droplets) now give a quantitative language for P granules, nucleoli and stress granules. This is a clear case of physics ideas changing how a whole field of biology thinks, and it is original and broadly useful across complex systems.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule liquid-droplet work (Brangwynne, Hyman, Jülicher and co-authors) is the decisive experimental and conceptual step, and Jülicher supplied the theory of active droplets. The three-name configuration looks defensible, though others contributed to the later link to disease and to the theory of chemically active droplets.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation, and the framework is widely adopted. Debate continues about which cellular structures are truly liquid and what is functionally essential, so the interpretation is mature for the core concept but not settled in every application.
uncertainties: Whether all claimed condensates are genuine thermodynamic phases is still contested.
Credit between experiment and theory, and the role of other early contributors, may be disputed.
The subfield sits at the edge of physics and may raise a question of disciplinary fit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and survey propagation turned spin-glass ideas into algorithms and a theory of hardness for random constraint-satisfaction problems. They linked glassy phase transitions to computational complexity and connect directly to message passing and inference in neural networks and machine learning. The physical insight is original and the impact reaches computer science, information theory and statistical inference.
assessment.attribution: Mézard, Parisi and Virasoro developed the cavity method for spin glasses, and Mézard, Parisi and Zecchina introduced survey propagation for random satisfiability in 2002. Parisi already received the 2021 prize, which complicates how a fair configuration is drawn. The supplied pair is plausible but leaves out other contributors such as Parisi.
assessment.maturity: The spin-glass roots are decades old and well confirmed. The satisfiability results are rigorously supported in part, and the applications to inference and coding are established. The recognition may be seen as partly covered by the earlier spin-glass prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 spin-glass prize may weigh against recognising this area again.
Rigorous status of some one-step replica symmetry breaking claims is partial.
Whether the credit is better spread over earlier cavity-method work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, followed by the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moiré quantum matter. It is a clean, tunable platform for strongly correlated physics and has spawned a large new field with fractional Chern insulators and related states.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group realised the experiments in 2018 with Cao and co-workers. The theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, but Yuan Cao and other contributors, and parallel work from other groups, make attribution not entirely clean.
assessment.maturity: The experiments have been reproduced by many groups and the field is very active. The microscopic nature of the superconductivity is not settled, so the interpretation of the phases is still maturing, though the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconducting state is unresolved.
Credit to students and postdocs, and to other twistronics pioneers, may complicate the three-name limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The defect-mediated theory of two-dimensional melting, with the hexatic phase, is a classic of statistical physics. It extended the Kosterlitz-Thouless picture to positional and orientational order and has long shaped work on soft matter, liquid crystals and 2D materials.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) developed the theory building on Kosterlitz and Thouless, who were honoured in 2016. A prize for this follow-up would have to justify itself as a distinct discovery rather than an extension of recognised work, and the three-name split is reasonably clean.
assessment.maturity: The hexatic phase has been observed in colloids, liquid crystals and some 2D systems, and the theory is well tested, though the order of the melting transitions remains debated in simulations. It is very mature; timing is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is sufficiently separate from the 2016 prize.
The nature of 2D melting in simple fluids is still argued in simulations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter with cold atoms in optical lattices gives controllable many-body Hamiltonians, with the Mott-insulator transition, single-site imaging and Hubbard-model physics. It is a conceptual and technical step with lasting impact on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, and Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid to Mott insulator transition in 2002. Esslinger and Cirac are also credited, so a three-person selection leaves out a number of strong contributors and is somewhat arbitrary. Jaksch is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Very strong confirmation across many groups, and the programme is flourishing. Recognition is timely, although the practical advantage over classical numerics is still being established for hard regimes.
uncertainties: Five credited names exceed what a prize can honour.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes (BEC, laser cooling) may reduce novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides strong light-matter coupling with superconducting qubits, enabling readout, gates and the architecture of superconducting quantum processors. It is a foundational platform of current quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed it in 2004 and Wallraff et al. demonstrated strong coupling. Girvin's role is substantial, so choosing three of four is a judgement. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which partly overlaps in subject.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and extensive follow-up, with rapid technological development. Timing is plausible, though the 2025 prize may reduce the immediate need.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize for superconducting-circuit quantum effects.
Attribution among four credited names is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is a non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions, and the basis of modern computations for Mott transitions and correlated materials. It is conceptually elegant and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar's mapping to the Anderson impurity problem, are the decisive steps. Others, such as Müller-Hartmann and Jarrell, also contributed, so credit is not tightly bounded.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with three decades of validation and applications including DMFT combined with density functional methods. Its status is secure, but its quantitative accuracy for finite-dimensional systems remains an approximation.
uncertainties: Whether it counts as a discovery or a method for a prize is debatable.
Credit to Metzner, Müller-Hartmann and others is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new window onto supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly early-universe physics. The significance is high as a new observational band.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from large collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA), and the supplied three names cannot represent them fairly. Credit for founding the pulsar timing techniques is also diffuse.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is statistically significant but not yet a firm detection with confirmed individual sources, and the origin of the signal is not settled. Recognition looks premature.
uncertainties: The source of the background (binaries versus new physics) is unknown.
Collaboration-based credit makes a one-to-three-person award hard to justify.
Hellings-Downs correlation significance is still moderate.
